title: The Cost of Compression: A Rate-Distortion Limit on Factual Hallucination
abstract: arXiv:2609.12111v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Factual hallucination in closed-book question answering is often treated as a coverage problem: a model fails because the relevant fact is absent from its internal memory. This view misses a second source of error. Even when a fact has been observed, finite memory may force it to be stored only approximately. We study this effect through a simple coverage--compression model of factual recall. We consider an unstructured question-answering task with $N$ possible queries and $K$ possible answers. A learner observes $M$ training facts, compresses them into at most $B$ bits, and answers uniformly drawn test queries without retrieval. For a uniformly random ground-truth mapping, we prove $\mathcal{E} \geq \frac{M}{N}\delta^\star\!\left(\frac{B}{M}\right) + \left(1-\frac{M}{N}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{K}\right)$, where $\delta^\star(r)$ is the inverse rate-distortion function of a uniform $K$-ary source under zero-one loss. translated_title: 压缩的代价：事实性幻觉的率失真极限
translated_abstract: 闭卷问答中的事实性幻觉通常被视为一个覆盖性问题：模型之所以失败，是因为相关事实不存在于其内部记忆中。这一观点忽略了第二种错误来源。即使某个事实已经被观察到，有限的记忆也可能迫使其只能被近似地存储。我们通过一个简单的覆盖—压缩事实召回模型来研究这一效应。我们考虑一个具有 $N$ 个可能查询和 $K$ 个可能答案的非结构化问答任务。学习者观察 $M$ 条训练事实，将其压缩至最多 $B$ 比特，并在无检索的情况下回答均匀抽取的测试查询。对于均匀随机的真实映射，我们证明了 $\mathcal{E} \geq \frac{M}{N}\delta^\star\!\left(\frac{B}{M}\right) + \left(1-\frac{M}{N}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{K}\right)$，其中 $\delta^\star(r)$ 是均匀 $K$ 元信源在零一损失下的逆率失真函数。这两项分别对应……
tldr: 该论文证明了事实性幻觉不仅源于事实未被学习（覆盖缺失），还源于有限内存迫使已观察到的事实只能被近似压缩存储，并首次给出了幻觉率的一个率失真理论下界。
en_tdlr: This paper proves a rate-distortion lower bound on factual hallucination, showing that finite memory forces observed facts to be stored only approximately, so hallucinations arise from compression itself, beyond mere coverage failures.
